TRANSCATHETER AORTIC VALVE REPLACEMENT PROCEDURE NOTE

Procedure Date: fictional follow-up year, several years after the index surgical valve
replacement (see accompanying test harness for the assigned Service Date)

Indication: The patient, status post surgical aortic valve replacement with a Magna Ease
bioprosthesis placed several years earlier, now presents with structural valve
deterioration of the surgical bioprosthesis and worsening heart failure symptoms. Given
prohibitive surgical risk for redo sternotomy, the heart team recommended a valve-in-valve
transcatheter approach.

Procedure: Valve-in-valve TAVR was performed via right femoral arterial access. A balloon-
expandable transcatheter valve was advanced across the failing surgical bioprosthesis and
deployed under rapid pacing in good position within the existing surgical valve frame.

Device: SAPIEN 3
Implant Size: 23

Final angiography and echocardiography confirmed good valve position with no significant
paravalvular leak. Post-procedure hemodynamics showed a mean gradient of 10 mmHg across the
new transcatheter valve, substantially improved from the pre-procedure gradient of 41 mmHg
across the deteriorated surgical bioprosthesis.

Disposition: The patient was transferred to the recovery unit in stable condition.
